function: MADRL (enhanced MASAC) sets UAV excitation current weights (collaborative beamforming) and flight speed/direction; STAR-RIS coefficients come from simulated annealing, not learning. p. 8
system: 8 single-antenna UAVs as virtual array, STAR-RIS (energy splitting, 60 elements, UPA) on a rooftop, mobile ground users on both sides, 2.4 GHz. p. 4, 12
method: Multi-agent soft actor-critic with self-attention critic and adaptive velocity transition; centralized training, decentralized execution; reinforcement learning, 3000 episodes. p. 9-10, 12
data_channel: Custom simulator: LoS UAV-to-STAR-RIS, Rayleigh UAV-to-user and Rician STAR-RIS-to-user links, Gauss-Markov user mobility; no dataset or measurements. p. 5-6, 12
test_conditions: Single simulated urban environment, identical settings for all methods; performance reported for varying numbers of UAVs and STAR-RIS elements (60 to 100); no unseen-scenario test stated. p. 12-14
baselines: Learned: MADDPG, MASAC, single-agent SAC (SAL); non-learned: Random actions; all baselines use the same simulated-annealing ATSO control for the STAR-RIS. p. 12-13
metrics: Reward convergence, average transmission rate and total UAV energy consumption versus number of UAVs and number of STAR-RIS elements. p. 13-14
complexity: Big-O computational complexity for training and execution (execution O(NM + NR NC)) and space complexity, compared with MADDPG, MASAC and MAPPO. No runtime reported. p. 11-12
q1_support: p. 5: "the Rayleigh channel model is suitable for modeling" (UAV-to-user); p. 6 uses Rician for STAR-RIS-to-user. Custom simulator with textbook fading; no 3GPP model, DeepMIMO, or measured data is cited.
q2_support: p. 14: "we evaluated the performance of HMCD, MASAC, MADDPG, SAL, and Random algorithms under varying numbers of UAVs". This is a sweep of system size; the paper does not state that a trained model is tested on conditions unseen in training.
q3_support: p. 13: "Random: A non-learning baseline where each agent selects random actions from the action space"; p. 12: "MADDPG: A classical MADRL approach"; p. 14: "HMCD consistently outperforms all competitors" in transmission rate.
q4_support: p. 12: "During execution phase, the computational complexity reduces to O(NM + NR NC)"; p. 11 gives the O(...) training complexity of HMCD.
q5_support: p. 12: "We evaluate HMCD in a simulated low-altitude urban environment". Channels are generated by the authors' own simulator; no code or data link and no public dataset is given.
notes: Passes above_phy because the MADRL action a_m = {I_m, v_m, phi_m, omega_m} (p. 8) holds the excitation current weights of the UAV collaborative beamforming together with flight control, a physical-layer decision learned jointly with one above it. The STAR-RIS is set by simulated annealing (ATSO, p. 9), so the RIS design is not learned. Area 6 (aerial-link beam control) is chosen over 3 by the specificity order; reviewer to confirm. q3: MASAC is the base algorithm of HMCD (p. 9), so it is not counted as a learned baseline; MADDPG and independent SAC (SAL) are standard algorithms applied to the same problem, and Random is the non-learned baseline.
